source_refs.note: Book p. 164: the heading 8.5 Application of Binomial Theorem is printed with no text of its own (8.5.1 follows at once). The teaching introduction on this page is ours.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kitab yahan sirf heading deti hai aur seedha 8.5.1 par chali jati hai; yeh chhota sa taaruf (introduction) hamari taraf se hai.
Ab tak hum ne binomial theorem se \((a + b)^{n}\) ko expand kiya, yani algebra ka kaam. Ab hum isi theorem ko poore numbers (whole numbers) ke sawalon mein ek auzaar (tool) ki tarah istemal karenge. Teen qisam ke sawal aayenge: (1) kisi bari power ko kisi number se divide karein to remainder (baqi) kya bachega, (2) kisi bari power ka aakhri digit ya aakhri do digits kya hain, aur (3) yeh saabit karna ke koi expression kisi number se poora poora divide hota hai (divisibility).
Socho \(8^{100}\) kitna bara number hai: is mein 90 se zyada digits hain! Calculator bhi haar maan leta hai. Magar binomial theorem ki madad se iska remainder do teen lines mein nikal aata hai.
Sab sawalon ke peeche ek hi chaabi (key idea) hai: base ko (divisor ka multiple) \(\pm\) (chhota number) ki shakal mein likho, jaise \(8 = 7 + 1\) ya \(2 = 3 - 1\). Phir expansion ke aakhri term ke ilawa har term mein divisor maujood hota hai, is liye jawab sirf aakhri term tay karta hai. Yeh baat zehan mein rakh kar 8.5.1 shuru kijiye.
